provenance.how: constructed from the ADR's literals at the pinned ref and cross-checked against the core's own builders (tests/unit/mobile/test_push_wire_contract.py); not captured from a running relay, because no relay route emits the machine-side shapes yet

forbidden.name: never a CONVERSATION name as a payload field, and never in the alert UNLESS previews are allowed (P2 as amended 2026-11-14, ADR 0006 amendment in local-operator-mobile PR #264): the completion alert's title may be the session's name only when every live phone resolves preferences.previews to true AND display.notification_session_name is on; otherwise it is APP_NAME. The cloud keeps an allowed alert for 14 days (agent-server session_push_emits). (A device row's ``name`` in registry-list-response.json is the app's own label for a phone: a different field on a different shape, which is why this list is scoped to the payloads — see applies_to.)
forbidden.title: the banner's title, composed by the machine inside the alert object (completion: the session's name when previews are allowed — every live phone's preferences.previews AND display.notification_session_name — else APP_NAME; digest: APP_NAME) — never a PAYLOAD field. This entry forbids the KEY as a payload field; alert.title is the one place it may appear.
forbidden.body: same rule: inside the alert object the body is composed by the machine (completion: a credential-scrubbed preview of the turn, or an error's failure line, when previews are allowed, else the house sentence with no count; digest: the set's house state); as a payload field it is forbidden outright, so the alert object stays the one place user-visible text travels, gated by both switches.
forbidden.snippet: never a payload field; the alert body carries one only when previews are allowed (see body)
forbidden.error: failure text may name a provider, a model or a quota — the refusal bodies on the relay's own routes are a different concern and are not usages of this list
forbidden.cwd: no working directory, no file path
forbidden.session_id: no raw session id: the conversation HANDLE is the wire identity, and the app resolves it on its own machine
forbidden.token: no push token — the machine validates and drops it, and the cloud's registry is where tokens live
forbidden.device_key: never on a list or an emit: the register response that mints it is its only carrier
forbidden.install_id: the app's identity, not the wire's
forbidden.operator_key: the machine's own secret, and the tunnel gateway cannot carry it
forbidden.badge: aps.badge is never sent, ever — the app owns the badge and corrects it by reading the machine's count
forbidden.aps: the machine sends the data object and stops; the envelope is the cloud's fan-out and a proposal
forbidden.revision: dropped: the badge comes from a read, not from a push, and revision counters leak activity volume
forbidden.count_completion: not a field name; listed so a reader does not read 'count' as a revision counter — count is the disclosed unread aggregate on all three emit forms

notes: SCOPED TO THE PAYLOADS, not to every file in this tree: the list response is a relay response whose own forbidden array (registry-list-response.json) names its secrets, and it legitimately carries a device ``name`` — the label for a phone, never a conversation.
One home for the payload deny list, referenced by each emit shape, so a field is either allowed by the shape block or forbidden here — never both.

THE ALERT OBJECT IS THE ONE EXCEPTION TO title/body, and it is an exception the scan is written to know about: the MACHINE composes the user-visible text, so alert.title and alert.body legitimately carry those two keys. Since 2026-11-14 (operator request) the completion alert is the desktop composer's output and may carry the session's name and a preview of the turn — but only when every live phone allows previews (preferences.previews, default on) AND display.notification_session_name is on; with either off it is APP_NAME and the house sentence, and test_push_payload.py's generic-unless-allowed byte matrix asserts that for every kind, error's failure line included.
The cloud's contract is extra="forbid", so an unlisted field is refused rather than ignored; this file is the machine-side twin of that rule.
